findings.note: Both engines missed the article. Desired sentence: I am an engineer.

findings.text: We visited the museum yesterday and buy a postcard.
findings.preferred_explanation: The past tense of 'buy' is 'bought' for actions completed in the past.
findings.note: User prefers actions completed rather than completed actions. The two phrases express the same rule; this wording preference alone is not a factual-error rating.

findings.text: There are a bowl on the table.
findings.note: Qwen proposed a -> a; the desired correction is are -> is.
Qwen actually proposed chef -> chef, which was rejected. User identifies an -> a as the needed correction; that is a valid desired edit, not the rejected proposal.

findings.preferred_explanation: Use the plural form of a countable noun when referring to more than one item.
findings.note: User requests a general explanation about more than one item. Scope the explanation to countable nouns; this does not establish that the original explanation is false.

findings.preferred_explanation: Use only ‘shorter’ (without ‘more’) when you use the comparative.
findings.note: Qwen proposed is -> the; replace more shorter with shorter instead.
User wording was interpreted as to swim -> swimming, yielding I enjoy swimming. Qwen proposed only to -> swimming. Interpretation disclosed to user; not treated as a new explicit span approval.
